# Source escape under upper-four protection — analytical candidate

Status: OPEN, hand-derived before any new enumeration; independently accepted analytical theorem, prospective freeze and scientific verification pending. Integrated parent bc23cf44110e4d794ada59ae2b647599b5a19d42 (scoped cover-static closeout). No full reachability theorem or native acquisition mechanism is claimed.

## Domain and exact question

Use the closed cover-static domain: finite simple H with no isolated vertices, roots E(H), star M_v at each type v, all positive integer original multiplicities a_v, original palette A=sum a_v, source vertex-cover number3or4. Saturation G is a subgraph of H. Original floors are a_u+a_v on G-edges and1 otherwise. Every current label footprint is contained in some original star; current core hitting number is at most FOUR. Native edits toggle one label/root incidence and retain all these conditions; hidden incidences remain unchanged. Original domination supplies lower-three protection for every original protected hidden completion. No observation, access, outcome or commitment primitive is added.

For each original actual label x, write v(x) for its original type. A source escape event is the FIRST occurrence of either (V) an empty original label, or (X) an incidence on x at a root outside its original star M_v(x). Before this event every label is nonempty and a subset of its own original star. X is a footprint change relative to the ORIGINAL label type, not merely a deletion. Source escape is a necessary event on any first-vacancy route, not a sufficient condition for such a route.

Let B_v mean that H has a vertex cover of size<=4 excluding v. Covers may be nonminimum. Let T_v be the incident G-edge set at v.

## Exact first-escape gate

A first source escape is reachable iff at least one of these explicit certificates exists:

V(v): T_v is empty, and either a_v>=2 or B_v.

X(v,w,z): v,w,z are distinct, vw and wz are H-edges, T_v is contained in {vw}, and either a_v>=2 or B_v.

The certificate applies to ANY actual original label of type v. V deletes that label's whole star. X first deletes every root of that label except vw, then adds wz. Choose any deletion order; the first escape occurs at the final edit. X never empties its edited label. No other original label changes. The achieved costs are deg_H(v) for V and deg_H(v) for X (deg_H(v)-1 deletions plus one addition). These are construction counts, not a claimed globally optimal reserve cost.

## Necessity: normalize the first event, not the whole path

Take any safe finite path with a first escape. All earlier footprints lie within their own original stars and remain nonempty. Consequently no original saturated root can lose any original supporting label before the event: it initially has exactly its required a_u+a_v supporters, and no label originally outside those types has acquired that root. Original saturated traces are therefore intact.

For a V event on original type v, its label is emptied by deletion. Its saturated trace must be empty, so T_v is empty. Restore all other labels to their original stars in the state just after V. This only adds original incidences, preserves domination, increases support counts while preserving the fixed original floors and cannot increase the hitting number. Thus the single-label deletion state is safe. If a_v>=2 the remaining original copy supplies its type. If a_v=1, all active labels have types other than v; a cover of at most four labels is equivalent to B_v.

For an X event on original type v, consider its nonempty footprint F just BEFORE the new incidence r is added. F is contained in M_v, while F union {r} is contained in some original M_w and r is outside M_v. Distinct stars of a simple graph intersect in at most the single root vw. Hence F={vw}, and r=wz with z distinct from v,w. The intact saturated trace gives T_v subset {vw}. Restore all OTHER labels to their original stars at the pre-event state; the state with x={vw} stays safe by monotonicity.

If a_v>=2, a full original v-star remains and upper-four is automatic. If a_v=1, any at-most-four-label cover in this normalized state either excludes x, yielding B_v, or includes x together with at most three other original star types excluding v. Those types cover H minus vw. Adjoin w to them: this yields an H cover excluding v of size at most four, hence B_v. (The apparent alternative using a three-cover of H minus vw is therefore redundant.) This proves necessity without asserting that arbitrary later paths normalize similarly.

## Sufficiency and every protected hidden completion

For V, the stated condition makes the single-label empty endpoint satisfy upper-four. No saturated incidence is removed. Every nonsaturated root still has its other endpoint's positive original multiplicity, so floor1 holds. Every intermediate deletion state contains this safe endpoint incidence-wise, so floors and upper-four hold; each edited footprint remains a subset of its original star. The final deletion is the first empty label and no outside-star incidence appears.

For X, the singleton state x={vw} has upper-four from the remaining v-copy or B_v. No saturated root except vw can be incident to v, and vw stays. All nonsaturated losses leave the other type's original labels, so floors hold. Any deletion order reaches this singleton through supersets of it. Adding wz then preserves floors/upper-four and is dominated by M_w. It is the first outside-original-star incidence and no label has become empty. The same argument works for every original choice of x.

At every state, domination by original footprints prevents any new full-system cover of at most two labels: replace chosen current core labels by original containers, retaining hidden labels, to contradict the original protected lower-three condition. The current core cover supplies upper-four. This is uniform safety of the constructed path under original hidden completions, not a native means of selecting or committing that path.

## Cover-reinforced source-lock corollary

Call v cover-pinned when B_v is false: EVERY H vertex cover C of size<=4 contains v. Such a cover necessarily has at least two neighbors of v outside C. With zero such neighbors remove v; with exactly one, replace v by that neighbor. Either operation would give a cover excluding v of size<=4, a contradiction. Suppose every type v satisfies either deg_G(v)>=2, or a_v=1 and v is cover-pinned. Then no source escape and hence no first vacancy is reachable.

Proof. Strong saturated traces exclude both V and X. For a singleton cover-pinned v, B_v is false. The exact gate therefore excludes every escape. Equivalently, before any hypothetical first outside incidence the upper cover forces the unique original v-label to retain at least two private roots for whichever cover is selected; it cannot fit any other star. This corollary is sufficient for locking, not a necessary classification of all locked sources.

## Explicit static-but-unreachable case with an isolated saturation type

Let H=K6 minus edge45. Its only independent pair is45, so its unique cover of size<=4 is C=0123 and its source hitting number is4. Let G be the complete bipartite graph between {1,2} and {3,4,5}, with vertex0 isolated. Choose a=(1,1,1,2,1,1), so A=7.

Static reserve exists: I={3,4,5}, N_G(I)={1,2}, deficiency1. Its only member in C is type3, which has multiplicity2; hence it is eligible under the closed cover-static theorem. Counts n=(1,2,2,1,0,0) sum to6, preserve C, meet all original floors and admit a spare label.

Nevertheless no first vacancy is reachable. Every v!=0 has saturated degree at least2. Type0 is a singleton and cover-pinned: the unique C leaves both its neighbors4,5 outside C. The corollary applies. Thus static existence AND minDegree(G)<=1 is NOT sufficient on general pair-root carriers, even when minDegree(G)=0. The source may still admit safe deletions within original stars; no claim of a singleton native component is made.

If a_0 is increased to2, V(0) holds and deleting one original type0 label reaches a reserve while another remains. This sharp control distinguishes a genuinely usable weak type from one required for upper protection. The negative and positive examples are hand-derived; no campaign has run.

## Source-three and other controls

For H=K5-minus34, all singleton, G isolating0, B_0 holds through nonminimum cover1234; V(0) succeeds even though minimum cover012 cannot be kept. K5 with duplicated types and saturated K23 has all G-degrees>=2, so no first escape despite static reserves. H=K5 with a saturated star has degree-one donors and admits X certificates, illustrating that a source can escape via reassignment rather than immediate vacancy. X existence alone is not promoted to general reserve reachability.

## Retained limits

This exactly characterizes the first escape gate, not all components, subsequent transfers, first-vacancy reachability after X, exact repair/exchange/restoration, arbitrary carrier hypergraphs, missing source types, edit-cost optimality, termination or native acquisition. It gives a new sufficient lock and a strict counterexample to the five-type reachability generalization. Broad C3/general C4 remain OPEN. No next numerical results exist before prospective freeze.


## Degree-one carrier boundary

The requirement that w has a neighbor z distinct from v in an X certificate is substantive. On a two-vertex connected component of H, both endpoint stars equal the single root; no outside-original-star incidence can be added through that component. If its edge is saturated, none of its labels can be emptied either.

For a concrete separate hand-derived control, take H to be K23 with parts{0,1}/{2,3,4}, disjoint from edge56, take G=H and all seven source multiplicities2. Source hitting number is3. Static reserve exists via I={2,3,4}, N={0,1}, retaining original cover{0,1,5}; nevertheless no source escape is possible. Types0..4 have saturated degree>=2; types5,6 have degree1 but no third vertex z for X, while V is excluded by their saturated root. Thus merely checking for a replaceable weak type, without a possible new incidence, is also insufficient. This example explicitly includes equal source-star behavior without assigning a fresh label or adding a new root.

# Cover-aware static reserve on general pair-root carriers

Status: prospective analytical candidate, OPEN pending independent analytical review, prospective publication, declared verification and scientific closeout. No new scientific enumeration has been performed. Parent: de41f3857b4c81690526fd6c0381bae07d0c0270, the completed nonuniform five-type checkpoint.

## Intent and native domain

Extend static reserve availability beyond the complete five-type root graph without promoting endpoint existence to reachability or importing a native observer. Retain original positive floors, original palette and original-footprint domination. No geometry, new outcome rule, full-state sensor, acknowledgment or commitment premise is derived.

Let H=(V,E) be a finite simple root graph with no isolated vertices. Roots are the edges of H; type v has footprint M_v consisting of the roots incident to v. Source type v has a_v>=1 distinct original labels, each with footprint M_v. Let A=sum_v a_v and let q be the minimum vertex-cover cardinality of H. Restrict the protected application to q in {3,4}. These source stars need not all be inclusion-maximal; domination by an original footprint and domination by an original maximal footprint are equivalent. No source type is missing.

Fix a saturation subgraph G=(V,E_G), E_G subset E. The ORIGINAL floor at root uv is a_u+a_v when uv is in E_G and 1 otherwise. A static admissible core uses the same A labelled palette, permits empty footprints, has each current footprint contained in some ORIGINAL M_v, meets every original floor, and has core hitting number at most FOUR. This is the inherited upper-four endpoint constraint for sources of hitting number three or four.

A static reserve means at least one original palette label is empty. It means neither a native path nor an observer-accessible record. The source hitting number is q. Let S={v:a_v=1}. Let C be any specified vertex cover of H with |C|<=4; it need not be minimum when q=3. Choose any one actual ORIGINAL label at each type in C as its anchor; these |C| label footprints must remain identical at the static endpoint. This is an endpoint preservation requirement, not a statement about an intervening path.

## Theorem

For each prescribed C and each such actual anchor choice, an anchor-preserving static reserve exists if and only if there is a nonempty independent set I in G such that

    |I| > |N_G(I)|    and    I intersect S intersect C = empty.

Consequently an unrestricted static reserve exists if and only if such a pair (C,I) exists for at least one vertex cover C of size at most four. In particular, whenever any static reserve exists, some static reserve preserves an actual original cover of at most four labels, possibly not a minimum cover. The same C works for EVERY choice of one original anchor label per type in C. This does not assert that every C works, or that a reserve can be reached with those labels unchanged.

The witness has explicit counts

    n_v = a_v - 1[v in I] + 1[v in N_G(I)].

It saves |I|-|N_G(I)| labels. Thus any existence witness, however large its count changes, implies a unit-per-type decrease/increase witness. Existence depends on the profile only through the singleton set S; actual multiplicities greater than one do not change the answer, although original floors and other quantitative questions do change.

## Proof for prescribed anchors

Necessity. Take a static endpoint with the prescribed anchors and at least one empty label. Expand each nonempty current footprint to some containing original star; choose the given star for each anchor. Expanding preserves floors and the actual anchor cover: those unchanged |C| anchors already cover all roots. Empty labels remain empty. Let n_v be the resulting type counts. Then sum n_v<=A-1, n_v>=1 for v in C, and n_u+n_v>=a_u+a_v on each saturated edge uv.

Put d_v=max(a_v-n_v,0), p_v=max(n_v-a_v,0). Since sum d_v>sum p_v, the finite integer layer identities sum d_v=sum_{h>=1}|{v:d_v>=h}| and sum p_v=sum_{h>=1}|{v:p_v>=h}| imply a level h with |D_h|>|P_h|. For any saturated edge from v in D_h, its other endpoint w must have n_w-a_w>=a_v-n_v>=h. Hence D_h is independent in G and N_G(D_h) is contained in P_h. Thus I=D_h has |I|>|N_G(I)|. If v is in S intersect C, n_v>=1=a_v, so it cannot be in I. This proves necessity without presupposing a bound on the endpoint's count changes.

Sufficiency. Given (C,I), independence gives I disjoint from N_G(I), so the displayed n_v are nonnegative integers. If v is in C and I, eligibility ensures a_v>=2, hence n_v>=1. All other types in C also retain at least one label. On saturated edge uv, a decreased endpoint has an increased neighbor; no saturated edge has two decreased endpoints. Thus n_u+n_v>=a_u+a_v. Each nonsaturated root has an endpoint in C, whose retained anchor alone meets its floor 1. These anchors cover every root, giving hitting number at most four. Domination and original palette are respected by assigning active labels to the indicated stars.

For the actual assignment, leave each chosen anchor unchanged. There are n_v-1 remaining positions at every v in C and n_v positions elsewhere, totalling sum n_v-|C| <= A-|C|-1. Assign that many distinct original non-anchor labels to these positions; leave the rest empty. No fresh label is introduced and no label is assigned twice. The particular original identity selected as each anchor is immaterial. This realizes the claimed endpoint for every anchor choice.

## Proof of unrestricted equivalence

Start from an arbitrary static reserve with a cover of at most four CURRENT labels. Expand every nonempty footprint to a containing original star. The selected covering labels still cover all roots after expansion. The set C of their star types is a vertex cover of H of size at most four; repeated star types are removed on taking this set. Therefore n_v>=1 on C. No minimum-cover assumption is used. The same deficit-level argument yields an eligible (C,I), and the constructive direction replaces the arbitrary endpoint by one preserving ORIGINAL anchors of that C. This replacement is static; no native route from the source or between endpoints is implied.

## Sharp upper-cover control beyond five types

Let H=K6 with only edge {4,5} removed, source a_v=1 at all six types, and G be H with all edges incident to type 0 removed. The unique independent pair in H is {4,5}; hence its unique minimum cover is C={0,1,2,3}, q=4. Type 0 is isolated in G but belongs to C.

The only deficient independent set in G is {0}. To verify this directly: on vertices 1..5 the only nontrivial independent pair is {4,5}, with neighborhood {1,2,3}. A single remaining vertex has at least three neighbors; adjoining isolated 0 does not make either of those sets deficient (the pair plus 0 has sizes 3 and 3). Thus {0} is the only deficit, and its singleton type lies in C, so the theorem excludes a static reserve.

Deleting the type-0 label is a floor-valid, original-dominated endpoint, but all five remaining types are needed to cover roots {0,w}, w=1..5. Its hitting number is 5 and it is inadmissible. This is a direct counterexample to generalizing “isolated saturated type guarantees a static reserve” or using deficiency without the cover condition. It is not a search-derived claim.

With a_0>=2 instead, the same I={0} is eligible and deletion of one type-0 label leaves an original type-0 anchor. With G isolating 4 or 5 instead, a singleton deletion is eligible because these types lie outside C. These are algebraic positive controls, not executed experiments.

## The source-three distinction is essential

Let H=K5 minus edge {3,4}, all a_v=1, and let G isolate vertex 0 by removing all H-edges incident to it. Source hitting number is three and the unique minimum cover is {0,1,2}. No deficient independent set avoids those singleton cover types: among the remaining types {3,4}, the pair has exactly two neighbors and either singleton has two. Thus no static reserve preserves this minimum cover.

Nevertheless C={1,2,3,4}, I={0} is eligible. Deleting the type-0 label preserves those four actual original anchors, meets all floors and has hitting number four. Thus a reserve exists in the original upper-four domain. Restricting C to minimum covers, or silently replacing upper-four by upper-source-tau, would wrongly reject this case. This is a hand-derived control, not an executed enumeration.

## Original protected completions

The theorem concerns the inherited core criterion of original floors, original domination and upper-four protection. It also preserves every original protected hidden completion under the same fixed hidden incidences. To see the lower protection directly, if the new full system had a cover of at most two labels, replace each selected current core label by any original label whose original footprint contains its new footprint. Keep any selected hidden labels. This yields an original full-system cover of at most two labels, contradicting its original lower-three promise. The current core anchors supply the upper bound of four regardless of the hidden completion. Core floors imply the required full-root floors. This is an endpoint guarantee, not a realized transition or observer acquisition.

## Reduction and boundaries

For H=K5, minimum covers omit exactly one vertex, so some C avoids I intersect S exactly when I contains at most one singleton. The theorem therefore recovers the closed five-type STATIC criterion, including isolates through I={v}; it does not re-prove that family's reachability/cost theorem. If all a_v>=2, the cover condition is vacuous for every C, and existence reduces to an independent-set deficiency in G.

Changing the root graph changes both the available covers and the meaning of an isolated saturated type. The five-type reachability criterion “static and minimum degree<=1,” four-anchor PATH theorem and costs 4/8/13 are not generalized here. Arbitrary root hypergraphs with roots supported by more than two source types, missing source types, exact labelled exchange/restoration, committed progress, native observation/access/retained output, broad C3 and general C4 remain OPEN.

The preserved C3 source screens require a justified native input, carrier/initial correlation, action connection and accessible retained output. This endpoint theorem supplies none of those objects. Path A remains active; Path B closed. No physical derivation or full-stack closure is claimed.

## Analytical review status
An independent analytical reviewer accepted the initial upper-source-tau statement and then explicitly accepted the strengthened exact upper-four statement above, without enumeration. The raw ANALYTICAL_REVIEW.md preserves both stages and the mandatory distinction between minimum covers and covers of size at most four. The initial draft is retained as historical INITIAL_ANALYTICAL_DRAFT.md, not the final scope. No computational or scientific-closeout acceptance is implied.

# Nonuniform five-type reserve availability — prospective theorem draft

OPEN pending computational verification and scientific closeout. Independently accepted analytical theorem; no new scientific enumeration performed before freeze. Parent weak-trace closeout7c9b6dd2b6b77176cfe9db125ed18276cf513ba0. Same five pair-root maxima M_i, all10 pair roots, positive integer source multiplicities a_i>=1, original palette size A=sum a_i. A graph G sets saturated original floor a_i+a_j on edge ij and floor1 on other roots. Original maximal domination, upper-four protection and original hidden family fixed. Broad C3/general C4/native premises OPEN.

## Static criterion for arbitrary positive multiplicities
A safe static reserve exists iff either G has an isolated vertex, or there is an independent set I in G with |I|>|N_G(I)| containing AT MOST ONE type of source multiplicity1. Equivalent local witnesses for no-isolate five-vertex G:
1. Two degree-one types sharing a neighbor (a cherry), with at least one of the two source multiplicities>=2.
2. An independent triple I with neighborhood size2, with at least two of its three multiplicities>=2.

Necessity: expand each active label of a hypothetical safe static reserve to an original maximal container. The resulting type counts n_i are nonnegative integers with sum n_i<=A-1, and all pair floors hold. All pair roots have floor>=1, so at most one n_i is zero. Let d_i=max(a_i-n_i,0), p_i=max(n_i-a_i,0). Since sum d_i>sum p_i, the integral layer-cake identities imply there is h>=1 with |D_h|>|P_h|, where D_h={i:d_i>=h}, P_h={i:p_i>=h}. Each saturated edge from i in D_h forces n_j-a_j>=a_i-n_i>=h. Thus D_h is independent and N(D_h) subset P_h. Any type in D_h with a_i=1 has n_i=0, so at most one such type exists.

If G has no isolates, N(D_h) is nonempty. On five vertices an independent deficient set has size2,3 or4. Size2 has neighborhood size1 and is a cherry. Size3 with neighborhood1 permits any two of its members as a cherry, choosing at least one multiplicity>=2; size3/neighborhood2 is the triple witness. Size4 has neighborhood1 and also yields an eligible cherry. This yields the two stated local alternatives.

Sufficiency: for any eligible deficient independent I, set n_i=a_i-1 on I, n_i=a_i+1 on N(I), and n_i=a_i elsewhere. Saturated floors hold since every neighbor of a decreased type is increased; no saturated edge joins two decreased types. At most one n_i is zero, so all nonedge floors1 hold and at least four maximal types remain occupied. Their maxima admit an actual four-label cover; thus the static core is safe with fewer than A active labels. The omitted labels are retained as empty labels in the same original palette. An isolated vertex alternatively permits deleting one original label in4 toggles, preserving four anchors from other types.

## Exact reachability criterion and fixed protection
